Faint ghosted handwriting covers the ruled area. The candidate and inventory both attribute it to show-through from fol. 51, the recto of this leaf. It could instead be, or include, offset from the facing fol. 52. Mirror-reversed ghost text cannot settle this, because offset from the facing page would also appear reversed. The ghosting runs right to the bottom of the page. On fol. 51 the writing appears to stop lower down, at about 1350/1500 of that image's height, while fol. 52 is written almost to the bottom. Which side the ghosting comes from is therefore not established. Either way it is not text of fol. 51b.

There are minor stray marks not listed in the inventory. One is a small diagonal tick near native x 725, y 1605. Another is a faint dashed diagonal near x 1070–1125, y 2190–2250. A small curl sits near the bottom edge at about x 2794, y 4816. Isolated dots are scattered elsewhere. All look like debris or offset rather than writing. They are not legible and none appears to be a note or holding.

   ceremonies.
annotations: Four lines of cursive ink across the lower part of the page, at about y 3225–3465.

Small commas are added below the line in line 3, after '1-35' and after 'col.'.
Line 4 'ceremonies.' is indented.

Two leftward-pointing arrows are drawn on the facing fol. 143, in its left margin at about x 3190–3340. They point from beside the entries d.13(3) and d.13(4) back toward the ends of lines 1 and 3 of this note.

The heavily overwritten word(s) before 'Brāhmaṇa' in line 1 are unresolved. The source may read something like 'on an unpublished' with re-inking, or something else.

The division of the note between d.13(3) and d.13(4) is unresolved. The relation of this note to the 'Begins: Vṛṣādarvikulam...' line on fol. 143, which is linked by an arrow to the area around d.94(11), is also unresolved.

(6) A left-pointing return arrow below Vagalamukhīstotra, about [2900,3900,70,50].
